items.stem: State any three short-term sources of finance.
items.answer: Trade credit; Factoring; Short-term loans from commercial banks; Commercial paper
items.markingKey: Any three of: Trade credit; Factoring; Short-term loans from commercial banks; Commercial paper (1 mark each).

items.stem: State one difference between owners' funds and borrowed funds on the basis of security.
items.answer: owners' funds: no security is needed; borrowed funds: usually secured on assets
items.markingKey: 1 mark: owners' funds: no security is needed; borrowed funds: usually secured on assets

items.stem: Explain the following short-term sources of finance: (i) Short-term loans from commercial banks (ii) Trade credit.
items.answer: (i) Short-term loans from commercial banks: Cash credit, overdraft and bill discounting. (ii) Trade credit: Credit given by suppliers for purchases.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Cash credit, overdraft and bill discounting. (ii) Credit given by suppliers for purchases.

items.stem: Jain Brothers keeps ₹5 crore of profit in the business. Is it owners' funds or borrowed funds?
items.answer: Owners' funds
items.markingKey: (b) Owners' funds. Retained earnings belong to owners.

items.stem: Bose Enterprises issues debentures to the public. Is it owners' funds or borrowed funds? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Borrowed funds. Debenture holders are creditors.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Borrowed funds; 2 marks for the justification: Debenture holders are creditors.

items.stem:
Kapoor Agencies of Shimla needs funds to build a new plant and to buy raw material for the coming season.
(i) Classify the two needs. (ii) Suggest one suitable source for each.
items.answer: (i) Plant: fixed capital requirement; raw material: working capital requirement. (ii) Plant: equity shares, debentures or loans from financial institutions; raw material: trade credit, bank overdraft or cash credit.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Plant: fixed capital requirement; raw material: working capital requirement. (ii) Plant: equity shares, debentures or loans from financial institutions; raw material: trade credit, bank overdraft or cash credit.

items.stem: Which finance term is described here? "Funds raised through loans or borrowings, on which interest is paid and which must be repaid."
items.answer: Borrowed funds
items.markingKey: (c) Borrowed funds: Funds raised through loans or borrowings, on which interest is paid and which must be repaid.

items.stem: Das Stores issues preference shares. Is it an internal or external source?
items.answer: External source
items.markingKey: (c) External source. Share issue raises funds from outsiders.

items.stem: State any three merits of equity shares.
items.answer: Suitable for investors willing to take risk for higher returns; No fixed burden of dividend; Permanent capital; Provides credit-worthiness; Funds can be raised without creating a charge on assets; Democratic control
items.markingKey: Any three of: Suitable for investors willing to take risk for higher returns; No fixed burden of dividend; Permanent capital; Provides credit-worthiness; Funds can be raised without creating a charge on assets; Democratic control (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the merits of equity shares?
items.answer: Not suited to investors who want steady income
items.markingKey: (d) "Not suited to investors who want steady income" is one of the limitations of equity shares, not one of the merits of equity shares.
options: Funds can be raised without creating a charge on assets
Suitable for investors willing to take risk for higher returns
Not suited to investors who want steady income

items.stem: Explain the following merits of retained earnings: (i) Helps absorb unexpected losses (ii) Permanent source of funds.
items.answer: (i) Helps absorb unexpected losses: Reserves cushion bad years. (ii) Permanent source of funds: Profits ploughed back stay in the business.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Reserves cushion bad years. (ii) Profits ploughed back stay in the business.

items.stem: Investors in Kapoor and Sons will receive a fixed 8% dividend before any dividend is paid to owners with voting rights. Which source of owners' funds or alternative is described?
items.answer: Preference shares
items.markingKey: (a) Preference shares. Fixed preferential dividend.

items.stem: Varun wants an investment in Iyer Traders with steady income and priority in repayment over owners. Which source of owners' funds or alternative is described? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Preference shares. Fixed dividend and priority in repayment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Preference shares; 2 marks for the justification: Fixed dividend and priority in repayment.

items.stem: Which source of owners' funds or alternative is described? In each case give a reason. (i) Rao Stores issues shares whose holders vote at meetings and get whatever is left after all claims. (ii) Rao Stores keeps 40% of this year's profit in the business to buy new machines instead of paying it as dividend.
items.answer: (i) Equity shares: Voting rights and residual claim. (ii) Retained earnings: Ploughing back of profit.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Equity shares (ii) Retained earnings

items.stem: Kulkarni Enterprises issues shares whose holders vote at meetings and get whatever is left after all claims. (i) Which source of owners' funds or alternative is described? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Equity shares: Voting rights and residual claim. (ii) Any two of: permanent capital; no fixed burden of dividend; voting rights and control; residual claim on income and assets; higher cost and dilution of control
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: permanent capital; no fixed burden of dividend; voting rights and control; residual claim on income and assets; higher cost and dilution of control

items.stem:
The promoters of Gupta Stores want to raise ₹50 crore but do not want to lose control or carry a fixed burden of payment. The company has large accumulated profits.
(i) Which source suits them best and why? (ii) Give one limitation of this source.
items.answer: (i) Retained earnings: no dilution of control, no fixed burden, no explicit cost. (ii) Shareholders may be unhappy with lower dividends; it is uncertain and limited by profit.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Retained earnings: no dilution of control, no fixed burden, no explicit cost. (ii) Shareholders may be unhappy with lower dividends; it is uncertain and limited by profit.

items.stem: Bose Agencies raises ₹10 crore at a fixed 9% interest, repayable after seven years, with no voting rights to the holders. (i) Which source of owners' funds or alternative is described? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Debentures: Fixed interest and repayment make it debt, not owners' funds. (ii) Any two of: fixed rate of interest; debenture holders are creditors; no voting rights; interest is tax deductible; fixed burden of interest and redemption
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: fixed rate of interest; debenture holders are creditors; no voting rights; interest is tax deductible; fixed burden of interest and redemption

items.stem: State any three limitations of debentures.
items.answer: Fixed charge on the company; Burden of redemption; Reduces borrowing capacity
items.markingKey: Any three of: Fixed charge on the company; Burden of redemption; Reduces borrowing capacity (1 mark each).

items.stem: State one difference between debentures and shares on the basis of security.
items.answer: debentures: usually secured on assets; shares: not secured
items.markingKey: 1 mark: debentures: usually secured on assets; shares: not secured

items.stem: Explain the following merits of loans from financial institutions: (i) Financial, managerial and technical advice (ii) Increases goodwill of the borrower.
items.answer: (i) Financial, managerial and technical advice: Institutions also guide the borrower. (ii) Increases goodwill of the borrower: Other lenders trust a firm backed by the institution.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Institutions also guide the borrower. (ii) Other lenders trust a firm backed by the institution.

items.stem: Kulkarni Retail invites the public to deposit money with it for two years at 8.5% interest. Which borrowed fund is described?
items.answer: Public deposits
items.markingKey: (c) Public deposits. Deposits raised directly from the public.

items.stem: Verma Industries invites the public to deposit money with it for two years at 8.5% interest. Which borrowed fund is described? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Public deposits. Deposits raised directly from the public.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Public deposits; 2 marks for the justification: Deposits raised directly from the public.

items.stem: Which borrowed fund is described? In each case give a reason. (i) Sethi Traders gets cash credit against its stock from a bank in Agra. (ii) Sethi Traders invites the public to deposit money with it for two years at 8.5% interest.
items.answer: (i) Loans from commercial banks: Cash credit is bank lending. (ii) Public deposits: Deposits raised directly from the public.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Loans from commercial banks (ii) Public deposits

items.stem: Patel Traders wants funds quickly without making its plans public and approaches its banker. (i) Which borrowed fund is described? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Loans from commercial banks: Bank loans are timely and secret. (ii) Any two of: timely funds as needed; secrecy is maintained; flexible amount; generally for short periods; strict conditions
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: timely funds as needed; secrecy is maintained; flexible amount; generally for short periods; strict conditions

items.stem:
Bansal Agencies has stable sales and earnings. It needs ₹20 crore for ten years but its promoters do not want to give up control.
(i) Suggest a suitable source and justify. (ii) State one limitation of the source.
items.answer: (i) Debentures (or a long-term loan from financial institutions): fixed interest, no dilution of control, suits stable earnings. (ii) Fixed charge of interest even in bad years, burden of redemption, reduced borrowing capacity (any one).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Debentures (or a long-term loan from financial institutions): fixed interest, no dilution of control, suits stable earnings. (ii) Fixed charge of interest even in bad years, burden of redemption, reduced borrowing capacity (any one).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about borrowed funds is correct?
items.answer: Debenture holders are creditors of the company.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: Debenture holders are creditors of the company.
options: Debenture holders are creditors of the company.
Interest on debentures need not be paid in a year of loss.
Trade credit is a long-term source of finance.
Public deposits always require a charge on assets.

items.stem: Pillai and Sons buys stationery from a supplier and is allowed 45 days to pay. (i) Which borrowed fund is described? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Trade credit: Credit from suppliers on purchases. (ii) Any two of: convenient and continuous source; readily available to creditworthy firms; no charge on assets; limited amount; may induce overtrading
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: convenient and continuous source; readily available to creditworthy firms; no charge on assets; limited amount; may induce overtrading

items.stem: State any three international sources of finance.
items.answer: Commercial banks; International agencies and development banks; International capital markets: GDRs; International capital markets: ADRs; International capital markets: FCCBs
items.markingKey: Any three of: Commercial banks; International agencies and development banks; International capital markets: GDRs; International capital markets: ADRs; International capital markets: FCCBs (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is true of GDR but not of ADR?
items.answer: Currency: usually US dollars or other foreign currency
items.markingKey: (a) GDR: Currency: usually US dollars or other foreign currency. The other options describe ADR.
options: Currency: usually US dollars or other foreign currency
Who can buy: only American citizens

items.stem: Explain the following features of GDRs: (i) Can be converted into shares (ii) Issued in foreign currency against shares of an Indian company.
items.answer: (i) Can be converted into shares: The holder can cancel the GDR and hold the underlying shares. (ii) Issued in foreign currency against shares of an Indian company: The shares are held by a depository bank.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) The holder can cancel the GDR and hold the underlying shares. (ii) The shares are held by a depository bank.

items.stem: Nair Agencies receives a long-term loan from the Asian Development Bank for a power project. Which international source of finance is used?
items.answer: Loan from international agencies
items.markingKey: (d) Loan from international agencies. ADB is an international development agency.

items.stem: A foreign company issues rupee-denominated depository receipts to investors in India. Which international source of finance is used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: IDR. Rupee receipts issued in India by a foreign company are IDRs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying IDR; 2 marks for the justification: Rupee receipts issued in India by a foreign company are IDRs.

items.stem:
Reddy Agencies, an Indian company, wants foreign investors to buy into it without listing directly abroad. It is choosing between London and New York.
(i) Name the instrument for each market. (ii) State one difference between them.
items.answer: (i) London: GDR; New York: ADR. (ii) GDRs are traded outside the USA and open to investors in many countries; ADRs are traded in the USA and only Americans can buy them.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) London: GDR; New York: ADR. (ii) GDRs are traded outside the USA and open to investors in many countries; ADRs are traded in the USA and only Americans can buy them.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about international sources of finance is correct?
items.answer: FCCBs carry a fixed rate of interest until conversion.
items.markingKey: (b) Correct: FCCBs carry a fixed rate of interest until conversion.
options: FCCBs can never be converted into shares.
FCCBs carry a fixed rate of interest until conversion.
GDR holders have full voting rights.
ADRs are traded on the Bombay Stock Exchange.

items.stem: State any three factors affecting the choice of source of funds.
items.answer: Cost; Financial strength and stability of operations; Form of business organisation and legal status; Purpose and time period; Risk profile; Control; Effect on creditworthiness; Flexibility and ease; Tax benefits
items.markingKey: Any three of: Cost; Financial strength and stability of operations; Form of business organisation and legal status; Purpose and time period; Risk profile; Control; Effect on creditworthiness; Flexibility and ease; Tax benefits (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain the following factors affecting the choice of source of funds: (i) Purpose and time period (ii) Control.
items.answer: (i) Purpose and time period: Short-term needs use short-term sources; long-term needs use long-term sources. (ii) Control: Equity issue may dilute control; debt does not.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Short-term needs use short-term sources; long-term needs use long-term sources. (ii) Equity issue may dilute control; debt does not.

items.stem:

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true and R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem:

items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Debentures. (ii) Control (no dilution), tax benefits (interest deductible), financial strength and stability (can bear fixed interest).

items.stem: Das Enterprises sells its trade receivables to a factor for immediate cash. Classify the source of finance by period.

items.markingKey: (d) Short-term source. Factoring is a short-term source.

items.stem: Ananya wants an investment in Mehta Enterprises with steady income and priority in repayment over owners. (i) Which source of owners' funds or alternative is described? (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.

An equity-linked debt instrument issued in a foreign currency, carrying a fixed interest rate, that can be converted into shares at a predetermined price (foreign currency convertible bond).
A depository receipt issued in a foreign currency against the shares of an Indian company, listed and traded on a stock exchange outside the USA (global depository receipt).
A depository receipt denominated in Indian rupees, issued in India by a foreign company (Indian depository receipt).

items.stem:
Menon and Sons of Surat needs funds to build a new plant and to buy raw material for the coming season.
(i) Classify the two needs. (ii) Suggest one suitable source for each.
items.answer: (i) Plant: fixed capital requirement; raw material: working capital requirement. (ii) Plant: equity shares, debentures or loans from financial institutions; raw material: trade credit, bank overdraft or cash credit.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Plant: fixed capital requirement; raw material: working capital requirement. (ii) Plant: equity shares, debentures or loans from financial institutions; raw material: trade credit, bank overdraft or cash credit.

items.stem: Ahuja Traders takes a four-year loan from a bank for new equipment. Classify the source of finance by period. Justify your answer.
items.answer: Medium-term source. Loans for one to five years are medium-term.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Medium-term source; 2 marks for the justification: Loans for one to five years are medium-term.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the merits of retained earnings?
items.answer: Opportunity cost is often ignored
items.markingKey: (b) "Opportunity cost is often ignored" is one of the limitations of retained earnings, not one of the merits of retained earnings.

items.stem: Patel and Sons rejects a loan because the lender wants to approve all its future borrowings. Which factor affecting the choice of source of funds is considered? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Flexibility and ease. Restrictive conditions reduce flexibility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Flexibility and ease; 2 marks for the justification: Restrictive conditions reduce flexibility.

items.stem: Which borrowed fund is described here? "Instruments acknowledging a debt, issued to raise long-term funds at a fixed rate of interest."
items.answer: Debentures
items.markingKey: (c) Debentures: Instruments acknowledging a debt, issued to raise long-term funds at a fixed rate of interest.
